question: A 22-year-old primigravid woman comes to the physician for her first prenatal visit at 10 weeks' gestation. She has no history of serious illness. She has been using cocaine for the past two years. Without cessation of cocaine use, which of the following complications is most likely to occur?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cocaine use during pregnancy" -> "increased risk of placental abruption" -> "premature delivery" -> 80% CHAIN: "Cocaine use during pregnancy" -> "vasoconstriction of uterine blood vessels" -> "obstructed labor" -> 70% CHAIN: "Cocaine use during pregnancy" -> "disruption of fetal cardiac development" -> "congenital heart defect" -> 60% CHAIN: "Cocaine use during pregnancy" -> "interference with neural tube development" -> "neural tube defects" -> 50% CHAIN: "Cocaine use during pregnancy" -> "increased amniotic fluid production" -> "polyhydramnios" -> 80%
analysis: Cocaine use during pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of premature delivery due to its vasoconstrictive effects on the placental blood vessels, leading to poor fetal oxygenation and nutrition.
